objective: Commit the Gazebo worlds the scenario manifests name, make world_version resolve to a committed file at load instead of failing at run time, and commit the fixed occupancy map the household world is planned against.
decision_supported: Does every scenario manifest name a world this repository has committed, and does a manifest naming an unknown version fail at load rather than mid-run?
acceptance: The world_version field resolves to a committed file at load: validate_scenarios.py refuses a version with no committed file, so the failure is a validation error rather than a missing model URI discovered mid-run.
Two worlds are committed, because the manifests name two versions: WorkbenchSim-v0 for the twelve frozen tabletop scenarios and WorkbenchSim-v0.2 for the household room.
The household world names the shelf, the parcel bay and the inspection table as separate addressable entities, plus the removable obstacle the path-blocked variants use.
The two lights a low-light variant dims are separate named lights, so a scenario dims one and leaves the other alone.
No model uses an external mesh URI, so no asset licence review is implied.
A fixed occupancy map is committed with a YAML sidecar carrying a revision and a sha256 of the image, and the sidecar states what the map does not claim about dynamic obstacles.
python3 tools/scripts/sim_cli.py list shows every manifest resolving to a checked-in world version, and validate_scenarios.py reports the resolved versions.
The world files are versioned: the README states that changing geometry requires a new world_version and a re-freeze.
evidence: validate_scenarios.py: PASS, reporting both world versions resolve.

The failure path: removing WorkbenchSim-v0 from the map makes validate_scenarios.py exit with a RuntimeError naming the version, which is the load-time failure this issue replaces the run-time one with.
pytest tests/unit/test_world_versions.py: 17 passed, covering both worlds, the named entities, the map digest and the unknown-version refusal.
The map sidecar digest matches the committed PGM, asserted by test.
make docs, check_doc_references.py, ruff check and ruff format --check clean.
A full make test comparison against the unmodified main baseline showing the same pre-existing environment-blocked failures and no new ones.
stop_conditions: gz sdf -k would have to be run to claim the SDF is schema-valid; Gazebo is not installed here, so the tests parse the XML and assert structure and the pull request says a structural pass is not a physics pass.
A run would have to reach the gazebo evidence class; that needs a simulator and is not claimed.
A world would have to be regenerated from a mesh asset; no external URI is added, so no licence review is implied.
A write outside allowed_paths is required, especially to sim/scenarios/** or to the Revision D description.
data_classification: Repository-local SDF, PGM, YAML, Python and Markdown. No credentials, private data or unreviewed assets.
model_policy: Deterministic XML parsing, Python and pytest; no model inference and no network access added by this change.
risks_and_fallbacks: The SDF is structurally valid XML but has not been checked against the simulator schema. A version-specific element could be rejected by Gazebo Harmonic. That surfaces as a load error in the container job, which is where the simulator exists, and the world file is the only file to change.

The committed map is derived from the world poses by hand rather than generated, so it can drift from the world. The sidecar digest catches a changed image, and a future generator would make the derivation reproducible; that is recorded rather than implied.
Two worlds rather than one avoids re-freezing 36 manifests, at the cost of a second file to maintain. The README states why they are separate and that changing either requires a new version.
Rollback is a revert of this commit: world_version returns to being an unresolved string. Nothing reads the worlds yet, so no consumer breaks.
